According to the legend, Shennong discovered tea when leaves from a wild tea plant accidentally blew into his pot of boiling water.
Curious about the aroma, he drank it—and found it refreshing and beneficial, leading to the discovery of tea.
SAQ02:
Tea plants are shade-grown for a few weeks before harvest to boost chlorophyll and flavour.
The youngest leaves are hand-picked.
Leaves are steamed to stop oxidation, then dried.
Stems and veins are removed, leaving only the soft leaf material (called tencha).
The tencha is then stone-ground into a very fine powder, which becomes matcha.

SAQ05:

Merchants wanted the freshest tea to arrive first, which led to intense competition (known as the “tea races”). This pushed shipbuilders to design faster vessels—resulting in the creation of the clipper ship.
